headline: BARRICK FILES S-1 FOR 'AMERICAN BARRICK GOLD' NYSE IPO — Carlin, Cortez, Turquoise Ridge, Pueblo Viejo; Q4 2026 Target
snippet: Barrick Mining has filed an S-1 registration statement with the SEC to list American Barrick Gold Corporation (ticker: ABGC) on the NYSE, with a secondary listing on the TSX. The new entity holds four Tier One North American gold assets — the Carlin, Cortez and Turquoise Ridge mines in the Nevada Gold Mines JV, plus Pueblo Viejo in the Dominican Republic. Goldman Sachs, BofA, Citigroup and RBC Capital Markets are listed as underwriters; Barrick intends to retain a controlling stake and return net IPO proceeds to shareholders, with the number of shares and price range not yet set.

headline: ENDEAVOUR MINING Q3 FLOORS WITH MANA MINE DISRUPTION — Stock Falls 7%, 2026 Output Guided to Lower Half of Range
snippet: Endeavour Mining's (TSX/LSE: EDV) Q3 2026 results revealed a significant operational disruption at its Mana gold mine in Burkina Faso — a ramp subsidence that suspended underground operations and pushed 2026 group production toward the lower half of the company's 1.09–1.265 million ounce guidance range. The stock fell approximately 7% on the November 12 release as investors priced in a higher-cost, lower-output second half; Mana is Endeavour's highest-grade mine but also its most logistically exposed, with no confirmed remediation timeline disclosed.

headline: GOLD CLAWS BACK TO $3,990 AS SILVER HITS $51.88 — Technical Analyst Eyes $4,150 Resistance After $84 CPI Selloff
snippet: Gold has recovered roughly one-third of its $84.30 drop following Tuesday's hotter-than-expected US CPI reading, with spot gold near $3,987 and silver at $51.88. FXEmpire's technical analysis identifies $4,000–$4,050 as the key near-term resistance zone, with $4,150 as the upper target for a full recovery; the gold-silver ratio fell from 78.2 to 76.6 as silver's relative strength signals the bounce may have traction — but analysts caution Federal Reserve rate-hike pricing for December has not yet fully unwound.

headline: VAULT SHAREHOLDERS BACK GENESIS MINERALS MERGER 99.74% — Court Approval Nov 16; Combined ASX Gold Producer Due by Nov 26
snippet: Vault Minerals shareholders voted 99.74% in favour of the scheme of arrangement merging Vault with Genesis Minerals at a scheme meeting on November 11 — one of the highest approval rates in recent Australian mining M&A. The deal still requires court sanction scheduled for November 16, with implementation expected November 26 subject to remaining conditions. The combined entity will be a large-scale Australian gold producer operating across Western Australia.

headline: GOLDHAVEN IDENTIFIES 8,850 PPM TUNGSTEN AT MAGNO BC — New Zone Extends Cassiar District Target Beyond Historical Footprint
snippet: GoldHaven Resources has identified new high-grade tungsten mineralization at its district-scale Magno polymetallic project in BC's Cassiar District, with samples returning 8,850 ppm tungsten — well above the 1,000–3,000 ppm typical of economic tungsten exploration targets. The discovery expands the mineralised footprint beyond previously documented historical zones and comes as tungsten's status as a NATO-listed critical mineral adds strategic weight to any Canadian discovery of this grade.

headline: USA RARE EARTH Q3 EARNINGS LAND — Jefferies Holds $21 Buy Target But Stock Sits At $8.15; Profitability Path Questioned
snippet: USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) reported its Q3 2026 earnings on November 11 with the stock trading at $8.15 — roughly 75% below its 52-week high of $32.80 — while Jefferies reaffirmed a Buy rating with a $21 price target. The Motley Fool's post-earnings analysis highlights a critical unanswered question: with Serra Verde's Brazil-to-Pentagon shipments now underway, the volume and pricing needed to reach cash-flow breakeven remain unclear given weak rare earth oxide prices and the company's pre-revenue burn rate.

headline: GOLD X2 MINING EXTENDS QES ZONE DOWN-DIP AT MOSS GOLD — 258.4m At 0.97 g/t Au Confirms Open-Pit Expansion Potential
snippet: Gold X2 Mining (TSX-V: AUXX) drilled 258.4 metres at 0.97 g/t gold and 192.0 metres at 0.90 g/t gold in extension holes targeting the down-dip continuation of the QES Zone at its Moss Gold Project — results that confirm the mineralised system extends below the current pit shell and support open-pit resource expansion modelling. The broad, bulk-tonnage intercepts are consistent with a large-scale low-grade porphyry-style deposit and add continuity to previously intersected high-grade intervals at the resource base.

headline: SILVER AND PALLADIUM LEADING GOLD'S RECOVERY — Why Analysts See This Pattern As Warning, Not All-Clear
snippet: FXStreet's November 11 analysis highlights an unusual pattern in the precious metals bounce: silver is outperforming gold and palladium is recovering strongly — a combination that historically precedes either a dollar counter-trend reversal or signals speculative short-covering rather than fresh institutional buying. The analysis flags a higher risk of a 'false dawn' for gold bulls given unresolved December rate-hike expectations and argues investors should wait for a confirmed close above $4,050 before treating the bounce as a durable floor.

headline: RISING OIL COSTS NOW SQUEEZE GOLD MINING MARGINS FROM BOTH ENDS — Fuel 15-25% of Mine Opex as Gold Revenue Contracts
snippet: An analysis from TheOTrade identifies the November 2026 gold mining selloff as driven by simultaneous cost and revenue pressure: rising oil prices are inflating diesel costs that represent 15–25% of mine operating expenses, while falling gold prices compress revenue — a combination that creates outsized negative earnings leverage for producers and developers. The piece expects 10–30% further corrections in metals mining stocks and flags Barrick, Newmont and Kinross as the institutional bellwethers to watch for signs of sector stabilisation.

headline: FIRST MINING GOLD Q3 2026 RESULTS — Springpole Federal EA In Hand as Developer Advances Ontario's Largest Undeveloped Gold Project
snippet: First Mining Gold (TSX: FF) released its Q3 2026 results on November 13, with the key operational highlight being continued advancement of the Springpole Gold Project in Ontario following its federal Environmental Assessment approval in June 2026 — the largest permitting milestone for what would be one of Canada's most significant new gold mines. The results come as gold markets correct from record highs, with First Mining's pre-production status insulating it from near-term revenue pressure while increasing balance sheet risk if capital markets remain risk-off for junior developers.
